title: orch ticket v1
description: One ticket = one file .orch/tickets/<id>.json. Writers must produce valid tickets. Unknown fields are allowed everywhere (top level and nested) and every reader/writer keeps them unchanged. Every field added after the first release is optional, so older tickets stay valid. The core knows no add-on: add-on data lives only under ext.<add-on name> and is checked by that add-on's own schema (addon-manifest.md, ticket_ext). type and wake_at are gone: wait until a time with waiting_on {kind: time, until}; recurrence is add-on data under ext.

id.description: Random, e.g. t_7k3f9q. Same as the file name.

key.description: Optional. Short display key for people, e.g. DM1-12: the workspace code ([workspace] code in .orch/config.toml) at creation, '-', and a number from the workspace counter (.orch/ticket-counter.json) that is never reused. Set once at creation and never rewritten (a new code changes only later keys). The id stays the identity everywhere; every command that takes an id also takes the key, any case. Tickets made before keys have none.

started.description: The ticket was started by an agent at least once; cleared only when a person moves it to open or ready.

revision.description: +1 on every write. `orch ticket patch --if-revision N` is refused when it changed (no lost updates between agents and add-ons). Missing = 0.

waiting_on.description: Generic waiting. The core records it and never promises that something wakes the ticket (an add-on may). kind time needs until; the other kinds need ref.

ref.description: question: q1 · ticket: t_… · external: ws_…, wh_…, a person, a PR URL, free text

ext.description: One key per add-on (its manifest name) or tool. Each owner decides its own shape; an installed add-on's ticket_ext schema checks its key on every write. Others never change a key they do not own.

owner.description: Optional. The person who owns the ticket, free text (a name), e.g. 'Severin'. Not a login.

due.description: Optional. Due day, YYYY-MM-DD, no time and no zone.

note.description: Optional. Free note from people, shown on the ticket. Plain text.

done_when.description: Optional. What people want to be true when the ticket is done. Plain text.

summary.description: Optional. Where things stand, one or two plain sentences, kept current by whoever works on it. Used to start a fresh agent session.

changed.description: What changed, one or two plain sentences.

outcome.description: Optional. What changed and why, written when the work is done (orch ticket outcome). Shown on the ticket and on the Notes page. Readers ignore it when absent.

description.description: Optional. What the ticket is about, written by an agent from the person's text (orch ticket title --description). Never the person's words: shown and sent to agents as the agent's description, with description_by.

plan.description: Optional. Written by the agent for a Show plan first ticket (orch ticket plan): the goal and what is not included, in its own field. Never merged into the person's note.

title_auto.description: Optional. True while the title is only a placeholder (the first words of what a person wrote); the agent writes the real title (orch ticket title), which clears it. A person's own title edit clears it too.

plan_first.description: Optional. True when the person chose "Show plan first": the agent makes the plan (parent and steps), asks one question "Plan ready" and waits for the answer before work starts. Set at creation only.

parent.description: Optional. Id of the parent ticket (sub-tickets). Set at creation. Children are not stored on the parent: they are found by reading every ticket's parent.

work.description: Optional. The ticket works in a separate copy of the project (a git worktree made by orch, branch orch/<ticket>), kept for the life of the ticket. A record for people and other machines: it holds NO local path (those stay in the machine-local registry .orch/run/worktrees.json) and no code resolves a path from it. A single-repo workspace has one entry per machine; more repositories add entries.

branch.description: The branch the copy works on, orch/<ticket>.

base.description: The commit the copy was made from.

sub.description: The workspace folder below the git top folder ('' when the workspace is the top).

host.description: The machine that made the copy (same value as a session's host).

sessions.description: Optional. Agent sessions that worked on this ticket, one entry per agent and machine (host). A new run resumes the entry whose agent and host match; otherwise it starts fresh. No age limit. The gitignored run record (run.schema.json) holds only the claim.

verdicts.description: Optional. The signed verdicts that make this ticket Done (human-proof.md 'Done needs a signed verdict'): a list because a MAC can be checked only by the machine whose key made it, so two machines that both accepted keep both entries. A ticket with status done counts as Done on a machine only when one entry is that machine's own verdict1 MAC over the ticket's checklist AND the current entry of its verdict ledger; every other raw done is Review there. Written only by the core when a person's proven verdict (or an agent finish under the recorded agents_may_finish grant) makes the ticket Done.

kind.description: person = a proven verdict (page or terminal proof, the phone through its own signed channel, the dev test human); agent = an agent finished while agents_may_finish was effective.

nonce.description: Random, fresh for every signing, so equal decisions get different MACs.

person.description: Optional, only on a person verdict signed from #484 on, always together with at. Who signed, inside the MAC. Legacy entries lack it and cannot authorise a synced person history line.

at.description: Optional, with person. When the person signed, inside the MAC (the sync merge ties the person's history line to it).

mac.description: base64url HMAC-SHA256(human.key, "verdict1." + workspace id + "." + ticket id + "." + canonical JSON of {status: "done", kind, checks, nonce[, person, at]}); checks = sha256 hex of canonical JSON [[step id, text, done is true, wont_do is true], ...].

who.description: agent:<adapter name> (e.g. agent:my-agent) or human:<name>. Add-ons that write log as agent:<add-on name>.

ref.description: PR URL, commit hash, file path (a copied file lives in the gitignored .orch/tickets/<id>/evidence/), URL, the command line, or the note text

title.description: Optional short name shown instead of ref.

summary.description: Optional. One plain line: what came out of the step. Shown on the task row.

role.description: Optional. result = what was asked for; check = proof it works; support = anything else.

exit.description: Optional, command evidence recorded with `orch check record`: the exit code. Data only: orch never runs the command.

ran_at.description: Optional, recorded command: when it ran.

files_sig.description: Optional, recorded command: fingerprint of the work folder at that time (git folders only). A different fingerprint now = 'changes haven't been checked yet'.

output_tail.description: Optional, recorded command: the last 2 kB of its output, control characters removed. Text only.

state.description: Optional. 'doing' = someone works on this item now (by, at say who and since when). Absent = not started or done (see done).

wont_do.description: Optional. true = a person decided this step will not be done ("Won't do"). It counts as resolved for finishing the ticket, needs no evidence and is never done=true. Set and cleared only by a person; an agent can only ask (a question). Absent = a normal step.

reason.description: Optional, only with wont_do: one plain line, why. Cleared with wont_do.

wont_nonce.description: Optional. A random value fresh for every signed Won't do decision (or its undo); part of what wont_mac covers, so equal decisions get different MACs. See human-proof.md, Synced won't do.

wont_by.description: Optional, new Won't do decisions only, with wont_at. Who decided, inside wont_mac (record field person). Legacy decisions lack it and cannot authorise a synced person history line.

wont_at.description: Optional, with wont_by. When the person decided, inside wont_mac (record field at).

wont_mac.description: Optional. The receiving core's own wontdo1 MAC over this step's decision {check, wont_do, reason, text, covers, nonce[, person, at]} (human-proof.md 'Synced won't do'): written when a person's Won't do (or its undo) was made here with a proof. The sync merge keeps a Won't do only when this is also the CURRENT entry of the receiving core's ledger, never by the text of `by`. Informational for every other reader.

covers.description: Optional. The part of the ticket's done_when this task covers, quoted in plain words. Used for the 'Done when' coverage line; absent = the task is not linked to a part.

check.description: Evidence-based: done=true needs at least one evidence entry. wont_do=true (a person's decision) is resolved without evidence and excludes done=true.

title.description: Empty: the short address is shown.

status.description: Set only by the add-on that owns kind (refresh act); shown only while it is on.

thumb.description: A picture in the ticket's artifacts folder (add-on with preview = 'thumb').

via.description: Where the answer came from (free word, e.g. cli, web, phone). null while unanswered.

kind.description: Optional. plain (default) or <add-on>:<name>; the add-on with that prefix acts on the answer. The core only records it.

action.description: Optional, opaque to the core: data the asking add-on needs to act on the answer.

check.description: Optional. The checklist item this question belongs to.

via.description: Optional. Surface the change came from (free word).

code.description: Workspace code: 2-4 uppercase letters or digits, e.g. DM1, MEC.

token.description: A short free word (a-z, 0-9, -) naming the surface or channel, e.g. cli, web, phone. The core never lists the allowed values.

agent_name.description: An agent adapter name: a key of agents.json or a [agents.<name>] table in .orch/config.toml.

id.description: The agent tool's own session id. Never starts with '-' (it is passed as a command argument).

host.description: Host name of the machine where the session lives; resume only on the same host.
